hints: Look carefully at how skeletal structures work, every corner and end of a line is a carbon unless an atom like N is written there.
You can count 4 nitrogen atoms written as N, and 6 carbon atoms hidden at the corners of the cage.
Work out how many hydrogens each carbon must have to make 4 bonds, then simplify the full molecular formula to its smallest whole number ratio.
walkthrough:
**Read the skeletal structure**

Great start, let's decode the diagram together. In skeletal structures, we do not draw C or H. Each bend or end of a line is a carbon atom, and N atoms are shown explicitly.

Count them: $\text{N atoms} = 4$

**Count the carbon atoms**

Now trace round the cage. There are 6 line corners that are not N, so there are 6 carbons hidden in the skeleton.

So far: $\text{C}_6\text{N}_4$

**Add the hydrogens using valency**

Each carbon must have 4 bonds. In hexamine each carbon is joined to two nitrogens ($\text{N-CH}_2\text{-N}$), so each carbon needs 2 more bonds to hydrogen.

That gives: $6 \times 2 = 12$ hydrogen atoms

Molecular formula: $$\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{N}_4$$

**Simplify to the empirical formula**

Empirical means the simplest whole number ratio. All the subscripts 6, 12, 4 can be divided by 2.

$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{N}_4 \div 2 = \text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{N}_2$$

options.A: This divides too far. $\text{CH}_2\text{N}$ would come from dividing $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{N}_4$ by 6, but 4 does not divide by 6 to give a whole number. Empirical formulas must have whole number subscripts.
options.B: This is correct. The cage contains 6 $\text{CH}_2$ groups and 4 N atoms, giving molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{N}_4$. Dividing by the highest common factor of 2 gives the simplest ratio $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{N}_2$.
options.C: This miscounts the carbons. It keeps N as 4 but uses only 4 carbons. Tracing all the corners of the cage carefully gives 6 carbons, not 4.
options.D: This is the molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{N}_4$, not the empirical formula. It is correct for atom counting but you must still simplify 6:12:4 to 3:6:2.
